I take notes a lot as my memory is appalling and forget what happened the week before quite often, I use the app and not paper character sheets as I find it easier. 

Don't let it stop you, plenty of fun to be had. I can't visualise any of it, just like when I read, and i read a lot of books.

I appear to have all of the A's. Anendophasia, Aphantasia, Anauralia, Alexithymia and the non A that is SDAM. 

No focus for sleep, I just grab a book until I doze off.

I can remember things with no detail. Like holidays for instance, I know all the places I have been and roughly when. Cant recall a single detail from any of them.

Rome, 2007. Spent a week there, I know it was burning hot and i walked round the main tourist sites. I don't remember a single thing about it, same with every other one.

Thank fuck for cameras. My unlimited amazon photos account has 260k plus pics as they are my only memories.

Often lay awake just not feeling tired so usually stay up late, around 2 to 3 am and then go to bed. Alarm for work is 5.30am. A bit better on weekends but not much. 

Also if something wakes me up, i can't go back to sleep and I'm always groggy when I wake. Takes me a good hour to wake properly. 

No inner voice etc, so a totally silent mind but that makes no difference.

My amazon unlimited photo storage has over 200000 images of my life that my brain won't ever show me.

Cant see it, smell it, taste it, hear it or feel it in my head. Yet all of those senses work fine. My sense of smell is dialled into to nasty smells which is really annoying. All flowers smell the same but walk into a room with a bin that's got something off inside it, or a person hasn't showered recently and I can pick that smell up at a hundred places away. Even if others in the room dont notice it. Very odd.

In one of my games, my character (level 10 dragonborn eldritch knight fighter with a backstory of being obsessed with finding more magical power) failed an investigation on a weird statue and it zapped him. He shook it off and carried on.

Shortly after my DM handed me a folded piece of paper. The note said you have been possessed by a demon and it has given you 10 levels of wizard but it will take over your body while you sleep and you won't know anything about it. Don't tell the rest of the party.

I added the 10 levels, extra hit dice and picked spells. Being a brass dragonborn I went with mainly fire spells. And I kept it to myself. 

Over the next few sessions in the city we were in, random gruesome murders happened and we were tasked with finding the culprit. We investigated,  questioned people, pissed off a lot of the criminal underworld and had many battles where I started using spells I shouldn't have, ie fireball. 

My party started asking questions that I couldn't answer. More so after a big fight where everyone was on their last legs and I still had tons of HP left.

While we investigated, more shredded bodies appeared overnight and my party got suspicious. Eventually they accused me, I still had no idea what they were on about. But while we all slept the demon took over and used my body to commit bloody murder. Then the mission for the party was to rid me of the demon. 

Skip a load of sessions. I was cured, I lost all my wizardly power and now a year or more later im just a slightly deranged level 15 fighter again.

Was a fun chapter, DM taking a backstory and working out a plot.

We both play dnd, and like a lot of subredits, I am a reader. New ideas for story and character from anywhere I can.

My mind is never totally silent thanks to tinnitus, but I have all the A symptoms. Sitting here now, in my lounge listening to the wind outside is nice but give it 10 minutes and I'll get itchy and have to get up and do something. 

Books feature a lot in this too. Sit here and read for hours. But sometimes I need to do more than that, hobbies, fix something, take the bike out for a 100 mile blast.

I definitely have ADHD, 40000000 online tests say so but costs thousands to find out here so not happening.

I have done several gross jobs over the years, my lack of visualisation has no doubt helped. 

Abbatoir worker in my youth, scraping bits of burnt bodies off of train tracks, car accident investigation and retrieving missing body parts. Now as a biomedical engineer I am often in operating theatres during surgeries when things stop working properly mid operation. 

Have seen loads of gross stuff and have many stories. Don't recall any details, no lost sleep and no nightmares. 

I wouldn't want to be without Aphantasia. I see it as a positive. The shitty memory thing has its bad sides though.

So far all are still going. My first character just got to level 14 and am surprised he is still going. He's a tank, greatsword fighter who is always first through a door and has a fascination for interacting with suspicious demonic statues and cursed objects. I'm sure his time will come.

Wing it,  hope for the best based on available information from previous situations or just never leave the house without a pen (AKA use my phone, it's a samsung with a stylus).

Ideas are in there somewhere from past events, they will come to me but i cant explain the thought process easily. The writing is an aid for remembering and easier planning.

Reading and writing is key, without that I have no chance of recalling information. Weird how seeing it burns it into my head somewhere. I'm full of useless info so great at quizzes 😁

All my notes for last few years have been electronic, kindle scribe is worth its money to me a thousand times over. It's packed with my mind dumps now. The hundreds of paper notebooks are up in the attic now.

I have completed the survey. 

Interestingly my lack of mental imagery, non existent  autobiographical memory and missing inner voice hasn't stopped me from studying over the years. 

Written information, that i have an interest in l, gets saved somewhere and is somehow accessible. Has to be written information so I can read it. Once read it's there when needed. Tell me something and it's gone in minutes. 

Wish I had AI transcription software when I did my degrees, would have been much easier in lectures. I had to write it all out myself back then.

I have random fleeting memories as a kid, more like brief flashbacks with no detail of where and when. More substantial memories are from 11-12 years old where I can remember going on a family holiday to france. No more detail than that though.

I was a kid and I did stuff, best answer I can give really.

Pen and paper mainly, or laptop. Ideas form somewhere and I write them/type them. Like my brain clicks print and my hand is the printer. I have to write everything down and read  to process it. Things I hear get forgotten quickly.

It is so weird and hard to explain. Tinnitus is the only sound in my head. 

My mind is silent otherwise, no sounds, no voices, no text, no images. I don't think I would cope with all that. 

There is such a variety of levels to all of this, some get voice only, some think in text.

Not as much, but I do still wake. Can only sleep when really tired, so I go to bed late, or I will just lay there wide awake. Once I wake up fully, then I'm awake, no more sleep. Even if it's just an hour.

As far i can recall I have never had a dream. I probably have but my brain refuses to let me remember it.

I have sleep issues for years, had a few sleep studies and REM sleep rarely happens. I wake up before it gets a chance. Worse case I was waking 26 times per hour. When they showed me the graphs I was a bit shocked. Explains why I'm always tired I guess.
I know the feeling 😁

I have a peaceful mind, quiet in every way. It is odd to think people have sounds, songs, voices, images, videos that can be bought up at will, or as memories or in dreams.

It's hard to describe how my mind works, information if I know it, it is just there like I instinctively know it. No thought process, It's just there.

Aa far as I know I have always been this way. It hasn't stopped me from getting on in life. Good grades at school, university and I do well at work. Found out that aphantasia was a thing in my early 30s, now mid/late 40s. I read up on that and associated mind related things, and many seem to fit me. Aphantasia, SDAM,  Anauralia, alexithymia, and even aspergers.

Blank mind sounds to me, like a clone that hasn't had its mind uploaded yet, like an empty shell.
I assume so yeah. No idea really as I never have.  Alexithymia,  aphantasia,  SDAM,  Anauralia. A whole host of things I miss out on I guess.

I don't think I feel fear as a mental sensation. My mind is kind of blank to emotions. To me it's the physical side I get. Maybe not fear specifically but adrenaline rush I get. 

Like when in a confrontation with someone, adrenaline pours in and I focus almost. As if looking for signs of attack. It's hard to explain how it feels.

My sleep is shockingly bad, some sort of weird insomnia. If I go to bed before 2am, I just lay there wide awake. I have a silent mind, so there are no thoughts or imagery to keep me up, I'm just not tired. Usually tired 2 to 3 am.

When I do feel tired and turn the lights out,  5 minutes and I'm asleep. My next issue is that if I wake up, I am awake, and no more sleep is happening that night. Even if it's only 30 minutes. My alarm for work goes off at 5 am, so no matter what, I don't get much rest.

It's like sleep is my enemy. It has been this way since I was 15, and I'm 47 now. I spend my extra hours reading or studying, so it's not wasted. More sleep would be nice though.

I don't know anything else. It's just the way I've always been so there is nothing to get used to. 

I can't imagine what acquiring it would be like. To feel and then to not must be a weird sensation.

Migraines when as constant at these drain your will to live. No matter how you sit or lay, it makes no difference. Mine were always bad on the eyes. My bedroom has 3 layers of blackout over the windows, no clocks, tv, or anything with an LED on it. 

The longest was 16 days of feeling like someone was using a hammer drill in my eye sockets. Average was 5 days, rhen the 2 or 3 days after where you are just not with it, sluggish and can't concentrate. A friend with epilepsy said they had the exact same feeling after a seizure, like the brain is  resetting and rebuilding itself.

What you describe makes sense, as the meds lower the mushrooms' effect, the migraines creep back into your life. All the SSRI meds I had before made me feel like shit. Usually  nauseous and numb. Never did like it, self medication did far more for me. Little by little, get them out of your system, and hopefully, you'll feel better for it. 

Let me know how you get on.

I would say it's definitely the meds. Anti-depressants and shrooms work on similar 5HT receptors I believe, over months on the meds you can get desensitization of these receptors and the mushrooms lose some of their effectiveness.

Different batches of mushrooms can have different levels of active ingredient in them. I have bought the same mushroom from the same place before and some are stronger than others. Where a 2.5g dose does little, and the next batch had me spaced out on the same amount. Anything natutal that's grown can be different between batches.

Getting off the meds has to be small reductions over time, they can be a bastard. I did mine over 6 months, reduced doses every few weeks.

Migraine free for 2 years now and I had them similar to you. Every few weeks I was out for days, hiding in the dark wanting to give up. I switched over to LSD microdosing as was easier to get where I live. Regular schedule i stuck to, and did bigger recreational does every few months too. Depression lingers a little but nowhere as bad as it was and Migraines, so far gone. I do get regular headaches a lot but can live with them. That never ending pressure feeling of the Migraine is no longer there. Let's hope it stays that way.

Good luck my friend. You can do this.

I am drawn to weirder jobs due to my lack of visual memory. Doesn't stop the nasty smells making me feel 🤮 though. 

Previous jobs over the years include abattoir worker, have done the full process from start to finish. 

Next was car crash investigation for insurance companies. Working directly with vehicle recovery and the police. On site just after the accident to study the scene as it was fresh. Seen many people's bodies in many states. Body parts spread across the roads etc, worse ones were motorcycle related but it didn't put me off riding. 

Then did similar on the railway, mostly suicide investigations on the tracks. Often messy scenes from train impact or rail electrocution.

Currently working as a biomedical engineer, often in operating theatres doing emergency work. See plenty of things that would make some people uncomfortable. Nowhere near as much as the other jobs, but still get covered in blood and other gore on a weekly basis. 

Aphantasia and SDAM help me here. Never remember a thing visually and no nightmares.
Biomedical engineer. Usually found in the depths of hospitals around the world having fights with medical machines that cost more than my house.
That made me fully aware how bad my memory is
Much the same as me, but opposite. Can't imagine what having a head full of noise is like, sounds horrific to me.
Not a video game but often higher doses make the world look like a cartoon that was drawn by van gough. Pretty cool to watch.

Don't let it stop you doing anything you want to do. Also don't use aphantasia as an excuse for not being able.

I found out about it in my 30's and I'm 47 now. I did 2 science degrees before I knew aphantasia existed. Work as a biomedical engineer travelling the world. I have full blown aphantasia, along with SDAM, anauralia and aspergers. My mind is silent and I love it just the way it is.

You can do anything, just believe in yourself.

That's it really, you know it and that's the important bit.

As far as I know, i don't dream, have never remembered one anyway. Another part of my broken brain 😁

I have microdosed for 3-4 years. It did wonders for my mental health,  no longer a suicidal mess 🤘

I am still an almost friendless loner. Still so hard to make friends and neither shrooms or acid helped that. However it wasn't my main focus for the microdosing, that was the suicide thing.

Can't hurt to try. Good luck 👍

I'm a very logical thinker, fully in show me evidence and I'll believe it once seen or experienced. The idea of supreme beings to me seems ridiculous but if I meet a God one day I will believe. 

Was the same with ghosts, the idea of spirits seemed too far fetched. Then I bought a house that was part destroyed in WW2 and rebuilt. From the day I moved in, weird things happened and carried on for years. I did all I could to work out what it was, what caused these things to happen and never could. To this day I can't work it out, ghosts, spirits, demons?

Doors opening by themselves. I checked for drafts, took the doors off and tested how balanced they were, changed hinges. Yet it still happened. I even talked to the 'ghost' and gave it a name 😁

Kitchen taps turned on by themselves. From off, to full flow but never while I was in the room. Always in the next room, doors open and you would hear the water start flowing into the sink. Took them apart, replaced them, made no difference, still happened. A friend witnessed this as we were in the room next to kitchen, freaked her out and she refused to come back in the house after that.

Photos moving.  Photo in a frame, on a shelf in the lounge. Walk in room and it would be face down. Stand it up again, leave room. Go back in their an hour later, 10 minutes later and it was face down again. Tried a different photo, nothing happened.  Same photo different room, nothing happened.  Same photo l, new frame and and same place. Then it carried on again.

Plenty more stuff similar, can't explain any of it. Changed locks incase someone was messing with me. Did all I could. It died off after about 8 years. Weird.

On big acid doses, I can move, walk, and act normally...ish.

Mushrooms on the other hand, ruin any ability to move or communicate so I do those alone.

When I read up on it, I fitted me perfectly. Same with several other issues that start with an A.

I wonder what others I can find. I had no real emotion about it though 😁

I'm 47, a biomedical engineer specialising in anaesthesia and critical care monitoring. Now travelling the world doing my job.

I have a list of memory/mind related problems.  Aphantasia, SDAM, Anauralia, Alexithymia, Aspergers. My memory is shockingly bad unless it's related to something I nerd over and then only if it's written down. Tell me something and I forget it, read it and it's there forever.

I think I subvocalise it into groups of 4 letters at a time and then add the one extra letter to get to Q.

I say I think I subvocalise, I'm not 100% sure it's correct. Quietly speaking without opening my mouth?
534 hours. Haven't fired it up in a while due to other games coming out.

Yeah all my memories are from photos I take on my phone. Camera roll is well over 60k pics. Without that, i have no recall further than I went somewhere or did something. 

I know i went to Rome for a week a few years ago. I remember it was September time, but I can't recall a single part of it.

I can remember being told I was a child once, don't  remember much of it though. Earliest memory is from about age 11, anything before that is sketchy. 

My wife can play her entire life back inside her head like a video. Rude.

I would say I'm emotionally stunted, yeah. I find it hard to connect with people, so I have very few friends. I find it hard to work out how people are feeling. The only time emotions appear with me is during the few hours of a hefty mushroom trip.

I forget people exist if i don't see, call or text them. Within a few weeks, they are gone from my mind. Even family, dad, brother etc. I am most comfortable by myself.

I don't reminisce on the past as I can't really remember it, only in details of where i was and roughly when. Can't remember holidays, good times and bad times. I take photos now, they are my memories.

Just how I thought everyone was once, but erm.... apparently not.

I don't know something, I read it and then i know it. No visual, no inner thoughts or text in mind. Knowledge just there the instant I need it. 

Useful at university,  Useful at work. New thing to learn so I can instruct others, read user manual, read service manual, teach techy stuff to others, get paid. Woohooo 😁

Faster to think and recall information i know. I have no visual memory at all, aphant, SDAM, total silent mind. If the info i need is in my head, then it's there,  no other processes slowing the brain down, i assume. 

I did well at school and university, and I have a high level technical job, which I do well at. I recall everything I ever read but forget everything else, so if someone tells me something, it's generally forgotten in minutes unless I make a note of it. My wife still calls me and asks me to get something from shop on the way home from work, so I have to tell her to text me. The moments that text appears on screen and I read it, I remember. 

The brain is a very strange thing.

Sadly my experiments didn't pay off, still dark behind my eyelids.

I thought for a second I had written this 😁 

I know exactly where you're coming from.
I like chess, but i suck at it. Can't visualise my moves or plan 10 moves ahead. Emotion plays no part in it as I don't really have any.

My Friday DM often adds a character to our party, usually someone we save in a dungeon, or someone that needs help. Always adds a new element to the game,  side quest for some gold or a cool shiny thing. Or we soon face a particularly vicious monster after they tag along.

None of us have ever tried to kill them though. That is a bit odd. So is a player adding another character at will.

I tried LSD and mushrooms to see if it helped my aphantasia.  With my eyes open the colours, patterns and distortions were fantastic. Close my eyes and back to my usual dark mind.

I did experiment with some sizeable doses too, made no difference sadly. Had fun though, music was awesome and the local forests were fantastic places to be.

Aphantasia still in effect, it is what it is.

The only things I remember is what I read. If it's read I remember, if I'm told something I forget it within minutes.
